in_english.name: Alimah
in_english.meaning: Learned, knowledgeable, and skilled in education
in_english.long_meaning: Alimah is derived from the Arabic root 'a-l-m' signifying knowledge, wisdom, and learning. She is a possessor of knowledge, skilled in education and training, a faqihah, scholar, and distinguished learned person. In Islamic tradition, Alimah represents a woman of great intellectual and spiritual significance, embodying the values of knowledge, wisdom, and piety.

data.cultural_impact: The title "Alimah" signifies a learned and educated woman, who has made significant contributions to Islamic scholarship and has elevated her status within the Islamic community. This title holds great importance in Muslim societies, as education and knowledge are highly valued. The title also reflects the progressive and empowering role of women in Islam and highlights their significant contributions to the religious and intellectual growth of the Muslim ummah (community).
data.spiritual_significance: The title "Alimah" represents the pursuit of knowledge and understanding in the path of Allah, as taught in the Quran. In Islamic tradition, knowledge is considered a fundamental pillar of faith and a key to religious and moral growth. The title is not only a testament to the Alimah's dedication to her faith but also to her commitment to the betterment of her community through the dissemination of knowledge. The pursuit of knowledge is a noble endeavor in Islam and one that is greatly rewarded in both this world and the next. The Alimah's label not only signifies her spiritual commitment to Islam but also her role as a spiritual leader, teacher, and guide for her community.
